example.name: refactor_dry_violation
example.scenario: Refactor duplicated transport logic in the witness extension
example.user_request: Refactor the transport module to eliminate DRY violations

step.approach: Review the transport module for repeated patterns. Outcome: identify duplicate error handling and connection logic.
Create utility functions to eliminate duplication. Outcome: extracted functions for error handling and connection management.
step.analysis: Ensure the extracted functions have clear, single responsibilities

step.approach: Replace duplicated code with calls to the extracted functions. Outcome: cleaner, DRY-compliant code.
Run TypeScript compiler, linter, and tests to ensure no regressions. Outcome: code compiles without errors and all tests pass.

example.completion: The transport module now has centralized logic, eliminating DRY violations. All common patterns use the extracted functions, improving maintainability.

key_takeaways.takeaway: Extract common logic into reusable functions to eliminate duplication
Ensure extracted functions have single, clear responsibilities
Always run TypeScript compiler and tests after refactoring

example.name: apply_solid_principles
example.scenario: Apply SOLID principles to the extension module
example.user_request: Refactor the extension module to better follow SOLID principles

step.approach: Review the extension module for SOLID violations. Outcome: identify modules/functions with multiple responsibilities.
Split modules/functions that have multiple responsibilities. Outcome: each module/function has one reason to change.
step.analysis: Ensure separation improves testability and maintainability

step.approach: Use interfaces to make the module extensible without modification. Outcome: new protocol handlers can be added without changing existing code.
Inject dependencies instead of creating them internally. Outcome: better testability and flexibility.
Run TypeScript compiler, linter, and tests to ensure no regressions. Outcome: code compiles without errors and all tests pass.

example.completion: The extension module now follows SOLID principles: - Each module has a single responsibility - The module is open for extension, closed for modification - Dependencies are properly inverted

key_takeaways.takeaway: Apply SOLID principles incrementally, validating after each change

example.name: improve_type_safety
example.scenario: Improve type safety by replacing 'any' with proper types
example.user_request: Fix type safety issues in the types module - remove 'any' types

step.approach: Review the types module for 'any' usage. Outcome: list of locations where 'any' is used.
Create interfaces or types to replace 'any'. Outcome: type-safe definitions for all data structures.
step.analysis: Use 'unknown' for truly dynamic data, specific types otherwise

step.approach: Replace 'any' with proper types throughout the module. Outcome: fully type-safe code.
Run TypeScript compiler to catch any remaining issues. Outcome: code compiles with strict type checking enabled.

example.completion: The types module is now fully type-safe: - All 'any' types replaced with proper types - 'unknown' used where dynamic data is truly needed - TypeScript compiler passes with strict mode

key_takeaways.takeaway: Define proper types for all data structures
Enable strict TypeScript checking for maximum safety
